neighbours.label: the word right after a citing verb that introduces the cited source (cited a, cites another, homage to); the same frame with a non-citing verb stays low
fire: In her lecture, Patel (2010) cited a report by the health ministry.
The editorial cites a poll taken by the local newspaper.
Their article had cited another paper from the same journal.
The final scene is a clear homage to Hitchcock's thrillers.
The judge cited a ruling from the previous decade.
Critics noted that the author cites several surveys from the 1990s.
The new album pays homage to the soul singers of Detroit.
Martin and Cole (2003) cited an experiment by Hughes on memory.
quiet: In her lecture, Patel (2010) wrote a report for the health ministry.
The editorial praises a park built by the local council.
Their article had missed another deadline from the same journal.
The final scene is a clear contrast with the opening chase.
The judge issued a ruling from the bench on Friday.
Critics noted that the author drives several cars from the 1990s.
The new album sounds close to the soul singers of Detroit.
Martin and Cole (2003) designed an experiment with Hughes on memory.

short: source introduced after a citing verb
notes: Card peaks ' a', '"', ' to', ' with', ' as' after cited/cites/homage/states. Probe: 'cited a study' 0.691, 'cited another study from' 0.462, 'homage to' 0.307, 'cites a 2002 survey' 0.285, quote opener after 'states,' 0.197; 'ran a study' 0.075, 'had found another' 0.029.
